summary: Senmyo Naniwa works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a PhD from Savitribai Phule Pune University, studying under Genjun Sasaki, Mohan G. Dhadphale, J. R. Joshi, and Purushottam Vishvanath Bapat, and held posts at Bukkyo University and Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.
Sensho Kimura is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University from circa 1961 to 1971. He later served as a professor at Otani University from circa 1986 to 2009.

Sensho Murakami was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University and Toyo University under Yukitada Takeda, Ryobun, and Gokan Un'ei. He taught at Komazawa, Otani, and Tokyo Imperial University, serving as professor at the University of Tokyo (1917–1923).

Seraphim Rose worked in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at San Diego High School, USC, California Institute of Integral Studies under Alan Watts, and UC Berkeley, later serving with the Russian Orthodox Patriarchal Parishes in the USA (~1962–1982).

Sergey Oldenburg was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Ivan Pavlovich Minaev at the University of Saint Petersburg. He served as professor at Saint Petersburg, director of the Asiatic Museum, and head of the Imperial Academy of Sciences (1900–1929).

Serinity Young was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. She completed her PhD at Columbia University in 1990 under Alex Wayman and Vidya Dehejia, later holding posts at the American Museum of Natural History and Southern Methodist University.
Sessō Oda was a figure in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Zuigan Goto from circa 1926 to 1935 and later succeeded him, teaching disciples including Sōkō Morinaga and Gary Snyder.

Seung-yeon Lee is a scholar in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology who studied under Lee Sang-hae. She has held posts at the Gyeonggi Institute of Cultural Properties and Sungkyunkwan University.

Seunghak Koh is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at Seoul National University and a PhD at UCLA in 2011 under Robert Buswell. He has served as an appointed researcher at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

Seungsahn Haengwon worked in Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at Dongguk University, he studied under Kobong Sunim, Keumbong, and Keum'oh, succeeded Kobong in 1957, and founded the Kwan Um School of Zen in 1970.

Seán McLoughlin is a religious studies and Indology scholar. He earned his PhD from the University of Manchester and served as Lecturer in South Asian, Islamic and Religious Studies at the University of Leeds (attested 2005).

Shailendra Bhandare is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He has held positions as curator at the British Museum, fellow at the Fitzwilliam Museum and St Cross College, and Assistant Keeper at the Ashmolean Museum (attested 2006–2022).

Shaman Hatley specializes in Indology and religious studies. Educated at Goddard College and the University of Pennsylvania under Ludo Rocher and Harunaga Isaacson, he taught at Concordia University (~2007–2015) and became chair of Asian studies at UMass Boston in 2015.
Shan Shan Zhao is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at McMaster University under the supervision of James A. Benn, also studying with Shayne Clarke and Mark Rowe.
Shanshan Jia is a scholar of Indology who studied as a doctoral student at the University of Hamburg under the supervision of Harunaga Isaacson (attested 2015).
Shaoyong Ye specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Peking University in 2009 under Qing Duan and served there as Associate Professor (attested 2010–2016).
Sharon J. Roe is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who completed her PhD at the California Institute of Integral Studies under the supervision of Steven D. Goodman (attested 2014).

Sharon Salzberg is a Buddhist and religious studies teacher. She attended the University at Buffalo and studied under teachers including Satya Narayan Goenka, Anagarika Munindra, Dipa Ma, and Sayadaw U Pandita, co-founding the Insight Meditation Society and Barre Center for Buddhist Studies.

Shashibhusan Dasgupta was a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Brojomohun College, Scottish Church College, and the University of Calcutta (MA, PhD), he served as a lecturer at the University of Calcutta from circa 1945 to 1964.

Shayne Clarke is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Bukkyo University, University of Canterbury under Paul Harrison, and UCLA under Gregory Schopen, later serving as Associate Professor at McMaster University (attested 2015–2016).
